title: 計測・制御工学
subtitle: Instrumental and control Engineering
educationalGoal: Students will: (1) Learn the basics of measurement (2) Learn the functions and roles of sensors (3) Learn the transfer functions of control systems (4) Learn the transient response method (5) Learn the basics of control system analysis based on the frequency response that is the basis of feedback control
advice: This is a basic course in instrumental and control engineering. We will cover the following topics: 1. Systems and their control 2. Basics of measurement 3. Specification of sensors 4. Standards and uncertainty 5. Types of sensors 6. Laplace transform 7. Transfer function 8. Block diagram 9. Board diagram 10. Stability of control system 11. Design of control system Students are expected to understand the concept of measurement. Students are expected to understand the meaning of the analysis method for control systems. Students are expected to determine the stability of a control system.
books: Textbooks: (in Japanese) Reference books: Reserved books:

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain how to select the signal that should be measured.
Be able to explain the traceability of measurement.
Be able to describe the results of measurement and their uncertainty.
Be able to describe an analysis model for a control system using the transfer function.
Be able to analyze the transient response and the frequency response for a control system.
Be able to identify regional issues.

achievementLevels.ideal: (1) Propose an effective method to select the signal that should be measured. (2) Explain the structure and necessity of measurement traceability. (3) Evaluate the uncertainty of a measurement. (4) Describe an analysis model for an automatic control system using the transfer function. (5) Analyze the transient response and frequency response for a control system and explain its characteristics. (6) Show concern for regional issues.
achievementLevels.standard: (1) Explain the necessity of signal selection in control measurement. (2) Explain the traceability of measurement. (3) Express a measurement result using significant figures. (4) Explain the transfer function. (5) Explain what is needed to determine the dynamic properties of a control system. (6) Show concern for regional issues.
